          Commencing on the 15th November, 2007/24 Kartika, 1929 (Saka)  

Obituary [15 NOV., 2007] References   1  
RAJYA SABHA  
Thursday, the 15th November, 2007/24 Kartika, 1929 (Saka)  
The House met at eleven of the clock, 
MR. CHAIRMAN in the Chair 
The National Anthem, "Jana Gana Mana", was played  
INTRODUCTION OF SECRETARY GENERAL, RAJYA SABHA  
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I have great pleasure in introducing to 
the House the New Secretary General, Dr. Vivek Kumar Agnihotri. 
OBITUARY REFERENCES 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound s orrow to the 
passing away of Shri Jana Krishnamurthy K., a sitti ng Member, Dr. L.M. 
Singhvi, Shri S.R. Bommai and Shri Jagdish Prasad M athur, former 
Members of the House. 
Shri Jana Krishnamurthy passed away on the 25 th  September, 2007, at the 
age of 80 years after a prolonged illness. Born at Madurai in the State of Tamil 
Nadu in May, 1928, Shri Krishnamurthy had his educa tion at Madurai and 
Madras Law College, Chennai. An advocate by Profession, Shri Krishnamurthy 
had engaged himself in several social and cultural activities right from his student 
days He won many laurels for his outstanding oratorical skills during his college 
days. He practised law in Madurai for more than a decade. Shri Krishnamurthy 
was the Vice-President of Bharatiya Janata Party for about 15 Years and rose 
to become is National President in March, 2001, and served that Party in that 
capacity til June, 2002 Shri Krishnamurthy represented the State of Gujarat in 
this House from April, 2002, till his sad demise. He was the Chairman of the 
Committee on Petitions from August, 2004, to Septem ber, 2006, Shri 
Krishnamurthy also had the distinction of serving as the Union Minister of Law 
and Justice from July, 2002 to January, 2003. In (h e passing away of Shri 
Jana Krishnamurthy K, the country has lost an able Parliamentarian, a noted 
lawyer and a distinguished social worker. 
Dr. L.M Singhvi passed away on the 6th October, 2007, at the age of 76 
years. Born at Jodhpur in the State of Rajasthan in November, 1931 Shri Singhvi 
had his education at Maharaj Kumar College Jodhpur; Maharaja's College, Jaipur; 
Jaswant College, Jodhpur; Allahabad University; Cambridge University, Harvard 
University; and the Cornell Unviersity. An eminent Jurist Dr. Singhvi was a multi- 

2   Obituary [RAJYA SABHA] References  
faceted personality. He served as the Advocate General of the State of Rajasthan 
from 1972 to 1977. He was the Chairman of the Rajasthan Law Reforms, Legal 
Services and Legal Aid Commission from 1973 to 1975, and of the Committee on 
Revitalisation of Panchayati Raj Institutions, Government of India in the year 
1986. Between 2000 and 2001, Shri Singhvi also served as the Chairman of the 
High Level Committee on Indian Diaspora and he conc eived the idea of an 
annual Pravasi Bhartiya Divas. Dr. Singhvi was elected President of the Supreme 
Court Bar Association of India several times, he conceived and founded the Law 
day, which is widely observed by the bench and the Bar in India on the 26th 
November every year. A seasoned diplomat, Dr. Singh vi, was High 
Commissioner of India in the United Kingdom from 1991 to 1997. An author, 
poet, publicist, linguist, literateur and patron of  arts, Dr. Singhvi was elected 
President of the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts in the year 2000 for ten 
years. He was also President and Chairman of the National School of Drama and 
President of the Authors Guild of India from 1977 to 1991. He was also President 
and Life Trustee of the India International Centre. A recipient of the Padma Bhushan 
in 1998, Dr. Singhvi was awarded U. Thant Peace Award in the year 1995. He 
was appointed one of the Presidents of the World Parliament of Religions held in 
Chicago in 1993. The legislative career of Dr. Singhvi started with the membership 
of the Third Lok Sabha, in which he was a Member fr om 1962 to 1967. He 
represented the State of Rajasthan in this House from July, 1998 to July, 2004. In 
the passing away of Dr. Singhvi, the country has lo st an eminent jurist, 
distinguished Parliamentarian, a renowned scholar, linguist and a connoisseur of 
art and culture. 
Shri SR. Bommai passed away on the 10 th October, 2007 at the age of 84 
after a prolonged illness. Born at Karadagi in Dharwad District of Karnataka in 
June, 1924, Shri Bommai had his education at Hubli Dharwad , Belgaum and 
Bombay University, Mumbai.' 
An advocate by profession, Shri Bommai participated  in the Quit India 
movement in 1942. He took part in various social movements even during his 
college days. Shri Bommai was associated with vario us social welfare and 
educational institutions in different capacities. 
The distinguished political career of Shri Bommai S tarted with the 
membership of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly in which he was a Member 
from 1967 to 1971, and, again from 1978 to 1939. He was also elected to the 
Karnataka Legislative Council in 1972 and remained a Member till 1978. Shri 
Bommai was the Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Council of Karnataka 
from 1976 to 1978 and in the Legislative Assembly of Karnataka from 1978 to 
1980. He was also the Chairman of the Public Accoun ts Committee of the 
Karnataka Legislative Assembly. 
He served as a Cabinet Minister in the Government o f Karnataka from 
1981 to 1983 and held portfolios of Industry and Co mmerce, Finance and 
Revenue, Planning and Institutional Finance and Irrigation. Shri Bommai also 
had the distinction of serving as the Chief Minister of Karnataka from August, 

Obituary [15 NOV., 2007] References   3  
1988 to April, 1989. Shri Bommai represented the State of Orissa in this House 
from July, 1992 to April, 1988 and the State of Karnataka from April, 1998 to 
April, 2004. He was Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and Forests from June , 
1988 to December, 1999 and the Committee on Petitions from May, 2000 to 
2001 Shri Bommai also served as a Union Cabinet Minister from June 1996 to 
March 1998 and held the portfolio of Human Resource Development. He was 
President of the All India Janta Dal from 1990 to 1996. In the passing away of 
Shri Bommai, the country has lost a distinguished p arliamentarian, an able 
administrator and a devoted social worker. 
Shri Jagdish Prasad Mathur passed away on the 20thOctober, 2007 at the 
age of 86 after a prolonged illness. Born at Sherkot in the Bijnor district of Uttar 
Pradesh, Shri Mathur had his education at the Mission High School and D.A.V. 
College, Dehradun. An educated social and political  worker, Shri Mathur 
participated in the Quit India Movement in 1942. He  was one of the founder 
members of the Bharatiya Janata Party. Shri Mathur represented the State of 
Uttar Pradesh in this House for two terms, from April 1978 to April 1984 and 
again from April 1990 to April 1996. He was also the Deputy Leader and Whip of 
the Bhartiya Janata Party in the Rajya Sabha. Shri Mathur was a Member of the 
Indian delegation to the Inter Parliamentary Union Conference held at Caracus in 
the year 1979. He also visited China as a Member of the Indian goodwill delegation 
of Parliamentarians. In the passing away of Shri Jagdish Prasad Mathur, the 
country has lost a distinguished social worker and an able Parliamentarian. 
We deeply mourn the passing away of Shri Jana Krish namurthy K., Dr. 
L.M. Singhvi, Shri S.R. Bommai and Shri Jagdish Prasad Mathur. I request the 
hon. Members to rise in their places and observe si lence as a mark of 
respect to the memory of the departed souls. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Secretary-General will convey to the members of the 
bereaved families our deep sense of sorrow and sympathy.
